result.description: Managed cloud database platform (MongoDB DBaaS); Admin API manages orgs, projects, clusters, users, backups, networking and more.
result.auth_detail: Service accounts (OAuth 2.0 client-credentials, bearer token ~1h) are recommended; legacy programmatic API keys use HTTP Digest auth. Credentials created per org/project by an org admin.
result.access_detail: Free Atlas account signup; org owner creates service account or API key in Atlas UI. Admin API has no documented paid-plan restriction (not explicitly verified; M0 limits some endpoints). Optional IP access list may be required. API manages the platform only, not cluster data.
result.api_notes: Atlas Administration API v2, versioned via Accept header (e.g. application/vnd.atlas.2025-03-12+json) at cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2. Covers clusters, projects, orgs, users, backups, alerts, network, etc. Separate Data API / driver needed for data access; Admin API doesn't expose cluster data.

evidence.quote: Service accounts are the recommended method to manage authentication to the Atlas Administration API.
API keys are a legacy method of authenticating to the Atlas Administration API that uses HTTP Digest Authentication.
Service accounts provide improved security over API (Application Programming Interface) keys by using the industry standard OAuth 2.0 protocol with the Client Credentials flow.
You can create a service account in MongoDB Atlas and use its credentials for authentication.
The Atlas Administration API doesn't provide access to the data stored in your clusters.
Many Atlas Administration API endpoint URLs (Uniform Resource Locators) follow the format of `/api/atlas/<version>/groups/<GROUP-ID>/`, where `<GROUP-ID>` is your project ID.
A Model Context Protocol server to connect to MongoDB databases and MongoDB Atlas Clusters.
